claims.claim_vi: The source lists six messaging patterns: asynchronous request-reply (HTTP 202 Accepted for long-running backend work), publisher-subscriber (decouples senders from consumers), claim check (stores the payload and transmits a reference), priority queue (higher priority requests processed sooner), saga (data consistency across services without distributed transactions), competing consumers (multiple concurrent consumers on one channel, no ordering guarantee).
claims.verified_by: Source body read at the pinned commit.

claims.claim_vi: Toy runs: three consumers over 12 messages with 1 to 9 steps each complete in the order 0,1,3,2,5,6,8,7,4,9,11,10; a priority queue serving one item per tick against 134 high-priority arrivals in 100 ticks serves 0 of 10 low-priority items and leaves 44 queued; a three-step saga failing at step three compensates in reverse (refund, then cancel booking); a 5 megabyte payload against an assumed 60-byte reference is about 87000 times smaller.
claims.verified_by: Run by the author on 2026-10-19 with small Python programs; the 60-byte reference size is an assumption of the experiment. Program: brainstorm/system-design-101-vi/experiments/sd-11-032.py (asserts the recorded values).

design_notes_vi: Một khung sáu thẻ cho sáu mẫu và một khung ghi chú kết quả thử.
source_deviations: The source gives each pattern a few sentences; the lesson keeps the six patterns in the source order and adds small runs that the source does not contain.
The author's runs are toy models; they illustrate a property, they do not measure a product.
The Microsoft catalogue was not opened in this session; the pattern descriptions rest on the source and on general knowledge.
